`osiris.cp.module` | All modules | Control Plane, All modules | **critical** | `module_id` |\n| `osiris.cp.health` | All modules | Control Plane | high | `module_id` |\n| `osiris.cp.command` | Control Plane | Target module | **critical** | `module_id` |\n\n### 4.2 Priority Queuing Model\n\n```\n┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│                    PRIORITY QUEUING                                  │\n├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n│                                                                     │\n│  Each priority level has a dedicated partition range per topic:    │\n│                                                                     │\n│  Topic: osiris.threat.alert (12 partitions)                         │\n│  ────────────────────────────────────────                           │\n│  Partitions 0-1:  CRITICAL  — threat alerts, IOC matches           │\n│                     → consumed immediately, no backpressure         │\n│                     → dedicated consumer pool (2 consumers)         │\n│                     → SLA: <100ms                                   │\n│                                                                     │\n│  Partitions 2-4:  HIGH      — threat scores, entity updates        │\n│                     → consumed within 500ms                         │\n│                     → shared consumer pool (3 consumers)            │\n│                     → SLA: <500ms                                   │\n│                                                                     │\n│  Partitions 5-7:  NORMAL    — intelligence events                  │\n│                     → consumed within 5s                            │\n│                     → standard consumer pool (4 consumers)          │\n│                     → SLA: <5s                                      │\n│                                                                     │\n│  Partitions 8-9:  LOW       — processed events, enrichment         │\n│                     → consumed within 30s                           │\n│                     → best-effort consumer pool (2 consumers)        │\n│                     → SLA: <30s                                     │\n│                                                                     │\n│  Partitions 10-11: BACKGROUND — raw SOC, heatmaps                  │\n│                     → consumed when resources available             │\n│                     → single consumer, low priority                 │\n│                     → SLA: <5min                                    │\n│                                                                     │\n│  Enforcement:                                                       │\n│  ─────────────                                                      │\n│  Producer sets priority in envelope.meta.priority                   │\n│  Event Router validates priority (CP can upgrade/downgrade)         │\n│  Kafka partition assignment uses priority-based hashing             │\n│  Consumers use prioritized fetch (critical first)                   │\n│  Backpressure: critical partitions always get throughput            │\n│                                                                     │\n└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n```\n\n### 4.3 Request/Response Pattern\n\nSome events require synchronous request/response (e.g., graph queries, AI inference). These use a correlation-based pattern:\n\n```\n┌──────────┐                    ┌──────────┐                    ┌──────────┐\n│ FRONTEND │                    │   EVENT   │                    │  ENGINE  │\n│   WS     │                    │  ROUTER   │                    │          │\n└────┬─────┘                    └─────┬─────┘                    └────┬─────┘\n     │                               │                               │\n     │ 1. Publish to request topic    │                               │\n     │ osiris.graph.query             │                               │\n     │ { correlation_id: \"req_abc\" }  │                               │\n     ├──────────────────────────────►│                               │\n     │                               │ 2. Route to engine            │\n     │                               ├──────────────────────────────►│\n     │                               │                               │\n     │                               │ 3. Engine processes           │\n     │                               │    (timeout: 30s)             │\n     │                               │                               │\n     │                               │ 4. Publish to response topic  │\n     │                               │ osiris.graph.result           │\n     │                               │ { correlation_id: \"req_abc\" } │\n     │                               │◄──────────────────────────────┤\n     │                               │                               │\n     │ 5. Route back to frontend     │                               │\n     │    (matches correlation_id)    │                               │\n     │◄──────────────────────────────┤                               │\n     │                               │                               │\n```\n\n---\n\n## 5. Scaling Strategy\n\n### 5.1 Kafka Cluster Scaling\n\n```\n┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│                    KAFKA CLUSTER TOPOLOGY                             │\n├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n│                                                                     │\n│  Phase 1 — Single cluster (3 brokers, 3 ZooKeeper/KRaft):          │\n│  ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────       │\n│  • 19 topics × 12 partitions = 228 partitions total                │\n│  • 3 brokers → ~76 partitions/broker (well within limits)          │\n│  • Replication factor: 3                                           │\n│  • Retention: 7 days (configurable per topic)                      │\n│  • Throughput target: 500K msg/s                                   │\n│                                                                     │\n│  Phase 2 — Multi-cluster (3 clusters, region-based):               │\n│  ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────       │\n│  • Cluster A: Real-time (critical + high priority messages)        │\n│  • Cluster B: Intelligence (normal + low priority messages)        │\n│  • Cluster C: Background (SOC raw + batch processing)              │\n│  • MirrorMaker 2.0 between clusters                                │\n│                                                                     │\n│  Partition count formula:                                           │\n│  ─────────────────────────                                          │\n│  partitions = max(                                             │\n│    expected_throughput / 10MBps,  // 10MB/s per partition         │\n│    num_consumers * 2,               // 2x consumer parallelism     │\n│    num_engines * 2                   // 2x engine isolation        │\n│  )                                                                  │\n│                                                                     │\n│  Example: osiris.soc.raw                                            │\n│  expected_throughput = 200MB/s (10M SOC events/day)                │\n│  partitions = max(200/10, 16*2, 6*2) = max(20, 32, 12) = 32       │\n│                                                                     │\n└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n```\n\n### 5.2 Consumer Scaling\n\n```\nConsumer Group per engine type:\n\n┌──────────────┬─────────────┬──────────┬───────────┬──────────────┐\n│ Engine       │ Consumer    │ Partition│ Processing│ Scaling       │\n│              │ Group ID    │ Strategy │ Model     │ Rule          │\n├──────────────┼─────────────┼──────────┼───────────┼──────────────┤\n│ GEOINT       │ geoint-cg   │ Range    │ Batch (1s)│ 1-4 consumers │\n│ Graph        │ graph-cg    │ Range    │ Request   │ 2-8 consumers │\n│ Threat       │ threat-cg   │ Range    │ Stream    │ 2-6 consumers │\n│ IOC          │ ioc-cg      │ Range    │ Batch     │ 1-3 consumers │\n│ AI           │ ai-cg       │ Range    │ Request   │ 2-16 consumers│\n│ Search       │ search-cg   │ Range    │ Request   │ 2-8 consumers │\n│ Fusion       │ fusion-cg   │ Range    │ Stream    │ 1-4 consumers │\n│ Workflow     │ workflow-cg │ Range    │ Batch     │ 1-3 consumers │\n│ Frontend WS  │ frontend-cg │ Range    │ Stream    │ 1-2 consumers │\n└──────────────┴─────────────┴──────────┴───────────┴──────────────┘\n\nAuto-scaling rules:\n  CPU > 70% for 5min → add 1 consumer (max ceiling)\n  CPU < 30% for 15min → remove 1 consumer (min floor)\n  Lag > 1000 messages for 2min → add 1 consumer immediately\n```\n\n---\n\n## 6. Failure Recovery Model\n\n### 6.1 Failure Scenarios\n\n| Failure | Detection | Impact | Recovery | RTO | RPO |\n|---------|-----------|--------|----------|-----|-----|\n| **Kafka broker crash** | Controller detects failed broker | Partitions on that broker unavailable | Automatic rebalance to remaining brokers | 10-30s | 0 (ISR with min.insync=2) |\n| **All Kafka brokers down** | All producers get timeout | No events accepted | Restart cluster, recover from persistent volumes | 2-5min | 0 (acks=all, flushed) |\n| **Consumer crash** | Consumer group rebalance | No processing for those partitions | Automatic rebalance, new consumer picks up | 5-15s | 0 (unprocessed messages stay in topic) |\n| **Schema Registry down** | Validation errors on produce | New schemas rejected, existing schemas cached | Restart registry, invalidate local caches | 30s-2min | 0 (schemas are immutable) |\n| **Redis Stream bridge down** | Bridge heartbeat timeout | UI events delayed, Python SDK events queued | Automatic restart, replay from Kafka | 5s-30s | Best-effort (UI refresh on reconnect) |\n| **Disk full (Kafka)** | Broker logs warning | Partition leadership lost | Auto-delete oldest segments (log retention bytes) | 1-5min | Retention period shortened |\n| **Network partition** | Producer timeouts | Some consumers isolated | Continue with available brokers; isolated consumers rejoin on recovery | Until network heals | 0 (Kafka requires ISR acks) |\n| **Corrupt message** | Consumer deserialization error | Single message skipped | Skip corrupted offset, move to DLQ for manual inspection | <1s | 1 message |\n\n### 6.2 Dead Letter Queue Architecture\n\n```\n┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│                    DEAD LETTER QUEUE                                 │\n├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n│                                                                     │\n│  Each topic has a companion DLQ topic:                              │\n│  osiris.intel.entity        → osiris.dlq.intel.entity               │\n│  osiris.threat.alert        → osiris.dlq.threat.alert               │\n│  osiris.geoint.processed    → osiris.dlq.geoint.processed           │\n│  ...                                                                │\n│                                                                     │\n│  DLQ Entry format:                                                  │\n│  {                                                                  │\n│    \"original_event\": { ... },          // Full original envelope    │\n│    \"error\": {                          // Error details             │\n│      \"type\": \"deserialization_error\",                              │\n│      \"message\": \"Invalid Avro schema version 3, expected 2\",       │\n│      \"consumer\": \"graph-cg-2\",                                      │\n│      \"timestamp\": \"2026-06-17T12:34:57Z\",                          │\n│      \"retry_count\": 3                                               │\n│    },                                                               │\n│    \"headers\": {                     // Original Kafka headers       │\n│      \"osiris.retry.count\": \"3\",                                     │\n│      \"osiris.max.retries\": \"3\"                                      │\n│    }                                                                │\n│  }                                                                  │\n│                                                                     │\n│  DLQ Management:                                                    │\n│  ──────────────                                                     │\n│  • DLQ retention: 30 days                                          │\n│  • DLQ consumers: manual investigation or automated replay          │\n│  • Alert threshold: >10 DLQ entries/min → pager duty alert         │\n│  • Automated replay: fixed DLQ entries can be re-published          │\n│                                                                     │\n└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n```\n\n### 6.3 Retry Strategy\n\n```json\n{\n  \"retry_strategy\": {\n    \"max_retries\": 3,\n    \"backoff\": \"exponential\",\n    \"initial_delay_ms\": 5000,\n    \"multiplier\": 2.0,\n    \"max_delay_ms\": 120000,\n    \"jitter\": 0.1,\n    \"retry_topic\": \"osiris.retry.{original_topic}\",\n    \n    \"retry_count_header\": \"osiris.retry.count\",\n    \"max_retries_header\": \"osiris.max.retries\",\n    \n    \"trigger_conditions\": [\n      \"consumer processing throws exception\",\n      \"consumer timeout (>30s)\",\n      \"downstream engine returns 503\",\n      \"deadlock detection\"\n    ],\n    \n    \"non_retryable_errors\": [\n      \"schema_validation_error\",\n      \"authentication_error\",\n      \"authorization_error\",\n      \"payload_corruption\",\n      \"event_too_large\"\n    ]\n  }\n}\n```\n\n---\n\n## 7. Observability Integration\n\n### 7.1 Metrics\n\n```json\n{\n  \"metrics\": {\n    \"event_bus\": {\n      \"events_produced_total\": { \"type\": \"counter\", \"labels\": [\"topic\", \"producer\", \"priority\"] },\n      \"events_consumed_total\": { \"type\": \"counter\", \"labels\": [\"topic\", \"consumer_group\", \"status\"] },\n      \"events_dlq_total\": { \"type\": \"counter\", \"labels\": [\"topic\", \"error_type\"] },\n      \"events_lag\": { \"type\": \"gauge\", \"labels\": [\"topic\", \"partition\", \"consumer_group\"] },\n      \"events_throughput_bytes\": { \"type\": \"histogram\", \"labels\": [\"topic\", \"direction\"] },\n      \"events_latency_ms\": { \"type\": \"histogram\", \"labels\": [\"topic\", \"priority\"] },\n      \"events_retry_count\": { \"type\": \"counter\", \"labels\": [\"topic\", \"consumer_group\"] },\n      \"consumer_group_members\": { \"type\": \"gauge\", \"labels\": [\"consumer_group\"] },\n      \"consumer_group_rebalances\": { \"type\": \"counter\", \"labels\": [\"consumer_group\"] },\n      \"broker_disk_usage_pct\": { \"type\": \"gauge\", \"labels\": [\"broker_id\"] },\n      \"broker_network_io\": { \"type\": \"histogram\", \"labels\": [\"broker_id\"] }\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n### 7.2 Distributed Tracing\n\nEvery event carries `trace_id` and `correlation_id`. Integration with **Grafana Tempo** (already deployed):\n\n```\n┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│                    DISTRIBUTED TRACING                                │\n├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n│                                                                     │\n│  Trace: osiris.investigation.paris_anomaly                          │\n│  ─────────────────────────────────────────────                      │\n│                                                                     │\n│  Span 1: soc.raw.ingested             [SOC Stream]     0ms ── 50ms  │\n│    ├── Span 2: soc.enriched           [IOC Engine]    50ms ── 200ms │\n│    │     └── Span 3: ioc.match.found  [IOC Engine]   120ms ── 180ms│\n│    ├── Span 4: geoint.point.added     [GEOINT Engine] 50ms ── 300ms│\n│    │     └── Span 5: geoint.heatmap   [GEOINT Engine] 200ms─ 500ms │\n│    └── Span 6: intel.correlation      [AI Engine]     300ms─ 1200ms│\n│          └── Span 7: threat.score     [Threat Engine] 800ms─ 1100ms│\n│                                                                     │\n│  Total trace duration: 1200ms                                       │\n│  Correlation ID: corr_01J2XYZ...                                    │\n│                                                                     │\n│  All spans exported to Grafana Tempo via OTEL                        │\n│  Trace view available in Grafana Explore → Tempo                    │\n│                                                                     │\n└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n```\n\n### 7.3 Alerting Rules\n\n```yaml\n# Prometheus alerting rules for event bus\ngroups:\n  - name: osiris-event-bus\n    rules:\n      - alert: HighEventLag\n        expr: osiris_events_lag{topic=~\"osiris\\\\.(threat|ioc|intel)\\\\..*\"} > 1000\n        for: 2m\n        labels: { severity: critical }\n        annotations:\n          summary: \"Event lag > 1000 on {{ $labels.topic }}\"\n\n      - alert: ConsumerGroupDown\n        expr: osiris_consumer_group_members == 0\n        for: 1m\n        labels: { severity: critical }\n        annotations:\n          summary: \"Consumer group {{ $labels.consumer_group }} has 0 members\"\n\n      - alert: DLQSpike\n        expr: rate(osiris_events_dlq_total[5m]) > 10\n        for: 1m\n        labels: { severity: warning }\n        annotations:\n          summary: \"DLQ spike on {{ $labels.topic }}: {{ $value }} events/min\"\n\n      - alert: BrokerDiskFull\n        expr: osiris_broker_disk_usage_pct > 85\n        for: 5m\n        labels: { severity: warning }\n        annotations:\n          summary: \"Broker {{ $labels.broker_id }} disk at {{ $value }}%\"\n```\n\n---\n\n## 8. Summary\n\n| Component | Technology | Purpose |\n|-----------|------------|---------|\n| **Primary event bus** | Apache Kafka (3 brokers) | Durable, replayable, ordered event streaming for all engines |\n| **Real-time bridge** | Redis Streams | Low-latency UI updates, Python SDK compatibility |\n| **Schema management** | Confluent Schema Registry (Avro + JSON) | Enforce event schema evolution |\n| **Dead letter queue** | Kafka DLQ topics | Capture and inspect failed events |\n| **Retry mechanism** | Kafka retry topics + exponential backoff | Automatic recovery from transient failures |\n| **Distributed tracing** | Grafana Tempo + OpenTelemetry | End-to-end event flow visibility |\n| **Metrics** | Prometheus + Grafana | Real-time event bus health monitoring |\n| **Bridge** | Control Plane Event Router (Go) | Bi-directional Kafka ↔ Redis Streams |\n\n**Key Design Decisions**:\n\n| Decision | Rationale |\n|----------|-----------|\n| **Hybrid Kafka + Redis Streams** (not NATS, not Pulsar) | Both already deployed; Kafka for durability/replay, Redis for low-latency UI; NATS adds operational complexity without enough benefit over existing infrastructure |\n| **Avro + Schema Registry** | Strict schema evolution, backward/forward compatibility, smaller serialized size than JSON; Confluent Schema Registry integrates directly with Kafka |\n| **Priority-based partitioning** | Critical alerts (threat, IOC) must never be delayed by background SOC ingestion; physical partition isolation guarantees throughput for high-priority flows |\n| **ULID for event_id** | Time-sortable, unique, URL-safe, no coordination needed (vs UUIDv4 which isn't sortable) |\n| **MirrorMaker 2.0 for multi-cluster** | Future-proofing for multi-region deployment without changing the producer/consumer API |\n| **Control Plane as bridge** (not standalone bridge service) | Avoids another service to manage; CP already has registry and event routing logic; single point of coordination reduces operational overhead |","operationIsLocatedInWorkspace":true,"startLineNumbers":[]}

## Key Design Decisions

| Decision | Rationale |
|----------|-----------|
| **Hybrid Kafka + Redis Streams** (not NATS/Pulsar) | Both already deployed; Kafka for durability/replay, Redis for UI; no new infrastructure |
| **Avro + Schema Registry** | Strict schema evolution, backward/forward compatibility |
| **Priority-based partitioning** | Critical threat alerts physically isolated from background SOC ingestion |
| **Control Plane as bridge** (not standalone service) | CP already has registry + routing logic; zero new services |
| **ULID for event_id** | Time-sortable, unique, no coordination needed |
| **19 topics × 12 partitions** = 228 total | Matches 6 engines × 2-3 topics each with headroom |HAS_CHANGES

You are a Principal Engineer designing a Plugin Engine for Osiris-Lab v2.

Context:
The system already contains tools, MCP servers, and engines inside /osiris but they are not unified or dynamically managed.

Your mission:
Design a Plugin Engine that turns every module into a dynamically loadable capability.

Requirements:
- Auto-discovery of plugins from filesystem
- Standard plugin manifest format
- Lifecycle management (load, unload, reload)
- Permission model per plugin
- Event subscription model per plugin
- Isolation between plugins

Design:
1. Plugin architecture model
2. Plugin manifest schema
3. Discovery mechanism
4. Execution sandbox model
5. Permission + RBAC mapping
6. Failure isolation strategy
7. Hot reload strategy

Constraints:
- Must support MCP-style tools
- Must not require system restart for updates
- Must scale to hundreds of plugins

     │  │ Controller    │  │ Enforcer             │    │   │\n│  │  └──────────────┘  └──────────────┘  └──────────────────────┘    │   │\n│ ┌──────────────────────┐    │   │\n│  │  │ gRPC          │  │ REST         │  │ Plugin Registry       │    │   │\n│  │  │ (Plugin Comm) │  │ (Management)  │  │ File Watcher          │    │   │\n│  │ Plugin Manifest Schema\n\n### 2.1 Canonical Plugin Manifest\n\nEvery plugin **must** include an `osiris-plugin.json` at its root:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"$schema\": \"https://[REDACTED:PASSWORD]@/workspaces/graph/GraphPanel\",\n        \"experimental\": false\n      }\n    ]\n  }\n}\n```\n\n### 2.2 Manifest Validation Rules\n\n```json\n{\n  \"validation_rules\": {\n    \"id\": {\n      \"pattern\": \"^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{2,63}$\",\n      \"unique\": true,\n      \"description\": \"Lowercase, hyphens only, 3-64 chars, globally unique\"\n    },\n    \"capabilities.id\": {\n      \"pattern\": \"^[a-z]+\\\\.[a-z]+$\",\n      \"unique_within_plugin\": true,\n      \"unique_across_system\": false,\n      \"description\": \"Domain.action format, e.g., graph.query\"\n    },\n    \"executor\": {\n      \"enum\": [\"go-native\", \"python\", \"nodejs\", \"docker\", \"wasm\"],\n      \"description\": \"Runtime executor type\"\n    },\n    \"events.subscribes\": {\n      \"items\": { \"pattern\": \"^osiris\\\\.[a-z]+\\\\..*$\" },\n      \"description\": \"Must match OSIRIS event naming convention\"\n    },\n    \"permissions.network.allow\": {\n      \"items\": { \"pattern\": \"^[a-z0-9.-]+:\\\\d{1,5}$\" },\n      \"description\": \"host:port format\"\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n---\n\n## 3. Discovery Mechanism\n\n### 3.1 Filesystem Scanner\n\n```\n┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│                    PLUGIN DISCOVERY                                  │\n├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n│                                                                     │\n│  Discovery paths (configurable):                                    │\n│  ──────────────────────────────────                                  │\n│  /osiris/plugins/              → Production plugins                  │\n│  /osiris/pkg/*/                → Go packages (auto-detect)          │\n│  /osiris/workers/*/            → Worker directories                 │\n│  /osiris/services/*/           → Service directories                │\n│  /osiris/intel/                → Intel server                       │\n│  /osiris/sensors/*/            → Sensor modules                     │\n│  /osiris/frontend/workspaces/*/→ Frontend panel plugins             │\n│  /data/osiris/plugins/         → User-installed plugins             │\n│                                                                     │\n│  Scan behavior:                                                     │\n│  ──────────────                                                     │\n│  1. Initial scan: on Plugin Engine startup                         │\n│  2. Watch scan: inotify/FSEvents on plugin directories             │\n│  3. Manual scan: POST /plugins/scan                                │\n│  4. Registry sync: periodic (every 60s)                            │\n│                                                                     │\n│  For each directory:                                                │\n│    1. Look for osiris-plugin.json                                   │\n│    2. If found → load and validate manifest                        │\n│    3. If not found → skip directory (no auto-inference)            │\n│    4. Check signature (if signed, verify)                          │\n│                                                                     │\n│  Deduplication:                                                     │\n│  ───────────────                                                    │\n│  plugin.id must be unique across all discovery paths               │\n│  If duplicate found → later registration fails                     │\n│  Version mismatches → CP decides which version wins                │\n│                                                                     │\n└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n```\n\n### 3.2 Registration Flow\n\n```\n1. FILESYSTEM EVENT (inotify)\n   ↓\n2. Scanner detects new/modified osiris-plugin.json\n   ↓\n3. Manifest Validator runs:\n   ├── JSON Schema validation\n   ├── ID uniqueness check\n   ├── Dependency resolution\n   ├── Permission validation\n   └── Capability conflict check\n   ↓\n4. On success:\n   ├── Store manifest in registry (etcd/Redis)\n   ├── Assign plugin instance (UUID)\n   ├── Emit event: osiris.cp.plugin.registered { plugin_id }\n   └── Notify Plugin Runtime Manager\n   ↓\n5. Plugin Runtime Manager:\n   ├── If auto_start: true → start plugin\n   ├── If auto_start: false → mark as \"available\"\n   └── If dependency not met → mark as \"pending_deps\"\n   ↓\n6. On start:\n   ├── Spawn appropriate executor\n   ├── Pass capability descriptor\n   ├── Register event subscriptions\n   └── Health check passes → \"running\"\n```\n\n---\n\n## 4. Execution Sandbox Model\n\n### 4.1 Executor Architecture\n\n```\n┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│                    EXECUTOR TYPES                                     │\n├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n│                                                                     │\n│  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │\n│  │  EXECUTOR: GO-NATIVE                                          │   │\n│  │  ─────────────────────                                        │   │\n│  │  • Compiles plugin as Go plugin (.so) via plugin package      │   │\n│  │  • Loads symbol: Lookup(\"Plugin\") → PluginInstance           │   │\n│  │  • Calls Init(manifest, eventBus) on load                    │   │\n│  │  • Runs in-process (same address space as Plugin Engine)     │   │\n│  │  • Memory isolation via Go runtime (goroutines, GC)           │   │\n│  │  • CGroup v2 per-plugin (memory, CPU limits)                  │   │\n│  │  • Crash isolation: recover() on panics, isolate goroutine    │   │\n│  │                                                               │   │\n│  │  Example: pkg/graph → compiled as graph-engine.so             │   │\n│  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │\n│                                                                     │\n│  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │\n│  │  EXECUTOR: PYTHON                                             │   │\n│  │         │   │\n│  │  • venv per plugin (isolated dependencies)                    │   │\n│  │  • CGroup v2 + process limits                                 │   │\n│  │  • Restarts on crash (up to max_restarts)                     │   │\n│  │                                                               │   │\n│  │  Example: workers/ai/main.py → Python executor                │   │\n│  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │\n│                                                                     │\n│  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │\n│  │  EXECUTOR: NODE.JS                                            │   │\n│  │  ────────────────────                                         │   │\n│  │  • Runs as subprocess, managed by Plugin Engine               │   │\n│  │  • stdin/stdout JSON-RPC for capability calls                 │   │\n│  │  • node_modules per plugin (isolated)                         │   │\n│  │  • CGroup v2 + process limits                                 │   │\n│  │                                                               │   │\n│  │  Example: intel/server.js → Node.js executor                  │   │\n│  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │\n│                                                                     │\n│  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │\n│  │  EXECUTOR: DOCKER                                             │   │\n│  │  ──────────────────                                           │   │\n│  │  • Runs as Docker container, managed by Plugin Engine         │   │\n│  │  • Docker Compose service definition in manifest              │   │\n│  │  • Full network/filesystem isolation                          │   │\n│  │  • Resource limits via Docker compose                         │   │\n│  │  • Health checks via Docker healthcheck                       │   │\n│  │  • Auto-restart via Docker restart policy                     │   │\n│  │                                                               │   │\n│  │  Example: services/event-bus → Docker executor                │   │\n│  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │\n│                                                                     │\n│  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │\n│  │  EXECUTOR: WASM (FUTURE)                                      │   │\n│  │  ─────────────────────                                        │   │\n│  │  • Runs as WebAssembly module via wasmtime/wazero             │   │\n│  │  • Strongest isolation (linear memory, no syscalls)           │   │\n│  │  • Portable across any runtime                                │   │\n│  │  • Ideal for MCP-style plugin tools                           │   │\n│  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │\n│                                                                     │\n└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n```\n\n---\n\n## 5. Permission + RBAC Mapping\n\n### 5.1 Permission Model\n\n```\n┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│                    PERMISSION MODEL                                   │\n├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n│                                                                     │\n│  Every permission is declared in the plugin manifest:               │\n│                                                                     │\n│  NETWORK                                                            │\n│  ├── Allow list: [host:port, host:port, ...]                        │\n│  ├── Deny list:  [host:port, ...] (override allow)                  │\n│  └── Wildcard:   [\"*:443\"] for HTTPS, [\"10.0.0.0/8:*\"] for subnet  │\n│                                                                     │\n│  FILESYSTEM                                                         │\n│  ├── Read paths:  [/data, /config, /shared]                         │\n│  ├── Write paths: [/data/plugin_id]                                 │\n│  └── Temporary:   [/tmp/plugin_id] (auto-cleaned on stop)           │\n│                                                                     │\n│  SYSTEM CAPABILITIES                                                │\n│  ├── Memory limit: max_memory_mb (default: 512)                     │\n│  ├── CPU limit:    max_cpu_cores (default: 1)                       │\n│  ├── PIDs limit:   max_pids (default: 256)                          │\n│  ├── Privileged:   cap_sys_admin (default: false)                   │\n│  └── Network:      allow_privileged_ports (default: false)          │\n│                                                                     │\n│  EVENT SUBSCRIPTION                                                 │\n│  ├── Subscribe to: [event_type_pattern, ...]                        │\n│  ├── Publish to:   [event_type_pattern, ...]                        │\n│  └── Rate limit:   max_events_per_second (default: 1000)            │\n│                                                                     │\n│  CAPABILITY CALLS                                                   │\n│  ├── Call other plugin capabilities: [capability_id, ...]           │\n│  └── Serve capabilities to: [plugin_id, ...] (empty = anyone)       │\n│                                                                     │\n└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n```\n\n### 5.2 RBAC Integration\n\n```json\n{\n  \"rbac_integration\": {\n    \"plugin_roles\": {\n      \"system\": {\n        \"permissions\": [\"network.allow:*\", \"filesystem.read:*\", \"filesystem.write:/data\", \"events.subscribe:*\", \"events.publish:*\"],\n        \"assigned_to\": [\"control-plane\", \"kernel\", \"event-bus\"]\n      },\n      \"engine\": {\n        \"permissions\": [\"network.allow:db:*,network.allow:broker:*\", \"filesystem.read:/config,/data\", \"events.subscribe:osiris.*\", \"events.publish:osiris.*\"],\n        \"assigned_to\": [\"graph-engine\", \"ai-engine\", \"geoint-engine\", \"threat-engine\"]\n      },\n      \"worker\": {\n        \"permissions\": [\"network.allow:broker:*\", \"events.subscribe:osiris.*\", \"events.publish:osiris.*\"],\n        \"assigned_to\": [\"graph-worker\", \"ai-worker\", \"geoint-worker\", \"threat-worker\"]\n      },\n      \"service\": {\n        \"permissions\": [\"network.allow:*\", \"filesystem.read:/config\", \"events.publish:osiris.intel.*\"],\n        \"assigned_to\": [\"intel-server\", \"osiris-brain\"]\n      },\n      \"sensor\": {\n        \"permissions\": [\"network.allow:*\", \"events.publish:osiris.soc.*,osiris.geoint.*\"],\n        \"assigned_to\": [\"shodan-sensor\", \"opensky-sensor\"]\n      },\n      \"tool\": {\n        \"permissions\": [\"network.allow:cp:*\", \"capability.call:engine:*\"],\n        \"assigned_to\": [\"mcp-plugins\", \"custom-tools\"]\n      },\n      \"untrusted\": {\n        \"permissions\": [\"network.deny:*\", \"filesystem.read:/data/shared\", \"capability.call:graph.query\"],\n        \"assigned_to\": [\"user-installed-plugins\"]\n      }\n    },\n    \"enforcement\": {\n      \"network\": \"iptables/nftables per Docker container or eBPF\",\n      \"filesystem\": \"bind mounts + read-only rootfs\",\n      \"capabilities\": \"seccomp profile per plugin role\",\n      \"resource\": \"cgroup v2 (memory, cpu, pids)\",\n      \"events\": \"Plugin Engine validates subscription against manifest\"\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n---\n\n## 6. Failure Isolation Strategy\n\n### 6.1 Isolation Boundaries\n\n```\n┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│                    ISOLATION BOUNDARIES                               │\n├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n│                                                                     │\n│  Level 0 — No isolation (Go-native, in-process):                    │\n│  ├── Go plugin system (.so files, plugin package)                   │\n│  ├── recover() on panic — single goroutine death                   │\n│  ├── Memory/cpu via cgroup v2 (per-plugin)                          │\n│  └── Suitable for: trusted core engines (graph, ai, geoint)        │\n│                                                                     │\n│  Level 1 — Process isolation (Python, Node.js):                     │\n│  ├── Separate OS process per plugin                                 │\n│  ├── stdin/stdout JSON-RPC communication                            │\n│  ├── Process death → Plugin Engine detects → restarts              │\n│  ├── OOM killer → only target plugin dies                          │\n│  └── Suitable for: workers, services, sensors                      │\n│                                                                     │\n│  Level 2 — Container isolation (Docker):                            │\n│  ├── Full Linux namespace isolation                                 │\n│  ├── Dedicated network namespace (no --net=host)                   │\n│  ├── Read-only root filesystem                                     │\n│  ├── Memory/cpu via Docker limits                                  │\n│  └── Suitable for: untrusted plugins, third-party integrations      │\n│                                                                     │\n│  Level 3 — Sandbox isolation (WASM, future):                        │\n│  ├── WebAssembly linear memory (no syscalls)                        │\n│  ├── Cannot crash host under any condition                          │\n│  ├── Deterministic execution                                        │\n│  └── Suitable for: user-installed plugins, MCP tools               │\n│                                                                     │\n└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n```\n\n### 6.2 Circuit Breaker Per Plugin\n\n```json\n{\n  \"plugin_circuit_breaker\": {\n    \"states\": [\"closed\", \"open\", \"half_open\"],\n    \"config\": {\n      \"failure_threshold\": 5,\n      \"success_threshold\": 2,\n      \"open_timeout_ms\": 30000,\n      \"max_timeout_ms\": 300000,\n      \"half_open_max_calls\": 1\n    },\n    \"triggers\": {\n      \"consecutive_failures\": \"Plugin capability call fails 5x in a row\",\n      \"crash_loop\": \"Plugin crashes >3x in 60s\",\n      \"health_timeout\": \"Health check fails >3x consecutively\",\n      \"resource_exhaustion\": \"Plugin exceeds memory/cpu limits\"\n    },\n    \"actions\": {\n      \"circuit_open\": {\n        \"effect\": \"All capability calls return 503 immediately\",\n        \"recovery\": \"Wait open_timeout_ms, then half_open\"\n      },\n      \"circuit_half_open\": {\n        \"effect\": \"Allow 1 test call\",\n        \"on_success\": \"Close circuit, resume normal\",\n        \"on_failure\": \"Re-open, double timeout (up to max)\"\n      },\n      \"circuit_permanent\": {\n        \"effect\": \"Plugin engine marks plugin as 'dead'\",\n        \"trigger\": \"Circuit opened >5 times in 1 hour\",\n        \"recovery\": \"Manual re-enable via API or manifest update\"\n      }\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n---\n\n## 7. Hot Reload Strategy\n\n### 7.1 Reload Triggers\n\n| Trigger | Detection | Behavior | Latency |\n|---------|-----------|----------|---------|\n| **Manifest file changed** | inotify watch on `osiris-plugin.json` | Re-validate manifest, apply new config | <1s |\n| **Plugin binary changed** | File watcher on compiled `.so` / script | Graceful stop, load new binary, resume | <5s |\n| **Configuration changed** | etcd/Redis watch on `/osiris/plugins/{id}/config` | Call plugin.Reload(config) | <500ms |\n| **Dependency changed** | Event `osiris.cp.module.registered` | Re-resolve deps, restart if required dep appeared | <10s |\n| **Permission updated** | Control Plane updates RBAC | Apply new iptables/cgroup rules live | <2s |\n| **Manual reload** | POST /plugins/{id}/reload | Full stop → wait (cooldown) → start | <30s |\n\n### 7.2 Hot Reload Flow\n\n```\n1. FILE CHANGE DETECTED (inotify on osiris-plugin.json)\n   ↓\n2. Plugin Engine receives event\n   ↓\n3. Lock plugin instance (prevent new capability calls)\n   ↓\n4. Run manifest validation:\n   ├── JSON schema → fail → reject, log error, do NOT stop running plugin\n   ├── Dependency check → fail → warn, apply partial changes\n   └── Permission check → fail → warn, keep existing permissions\n   ↓\n5. If validation passes:\n   ├── Stop event subscriptions (unsubscribe from Kafka/Redis)\n   ├── Call plugin.PreShutdown() (if applicable)\n   ├── Wait for inflight requests to complete (max 30s)\n   ├── Force kill remaining goroutines/processes (SIGKILL)\n   ├── Clear cgroup limits for old plugin\n   ├── Load new version:\n   │   ├── Go-native: dlopen new .so, resolve symbol\n   │   ├── Python: spawn new subprocess\n   │   ├── Node.js: spawn new subprocess\n   │   └── Docker: docker-compose up -d\n   ├── Start new version:\n   │   ├── Call plugin.Init(newManifest)\n   │   ├── Subscribe to events\n   │   ├── Register capabilities\n   │   └── Health check → pass → \"running\"\n   └── Unlock plugin instance\n   ↓\n6. Emit event: osiris.cp.plugin.reloaded { plugin_id, old_version, new_version }\n   ↓\n7. If reload fails:\n   ├── Old version should still be running (step 3 lock prevented new calls)\n   ├── Stop new version attempt\n   ├── Log error\n   ├── Emit event: osiris.cp.plugin.reload_failed { plugin_id, error }\n   └── Mark plugin as \"running_old\"\n```\n\n---\n\n## 8. Shared Data Schema (Entity-Centric)\n\n### 2.1 Master Entity Model\n\nAll engines share a single canonical entity model. Every intelligence object in the system is an Entity with a unique ID.\n\n```json\n{\n  \"osiris:entity:v2\": {\n    \"identity\": {\n      \"entity_id\": \"ent_01J2XYZ...\",          // ULID — globally unique, time-sortable\n      \"type\": \"domain\",                        // domain | ip_address | person | organization |\n                                               // location | threat_actor | malware | ioc |\n                                               // incident | event | asset | signal\n      \"subtype\": \"malicious_domain\",           // Domain-specific classification\n      \"label\": \"suspicious-domain.io\",         // Human-readable primary label\n      \"aliases\": [\"suspicious-domain.io\", \"45.33.22.1\"], // Known aliases\n      \"external_ids\": {                        // External system references\n        \"shodan\": \"shodan_123\",\n        \"virustotal\": \"vt_456\",\n        \"mitre_attack\": \"T1071\"\n      }\n    },\n    \"temporal\": {\n      \"created_at\": \"2026-06-17T12:00:00Z\",   // First seen\n      \"updated_at\": \"2026-06-17T12:34:56Z\",   // Last updated\n      \"last_seen\": \"2026-06-17T12:34:56Z\",    // Last observation\n      \"first_seen\": \"2026-06-17T08:00:00Z\",   // First observation\n      \"ttl_days\": 90                           // Auto-expire after (0 = permanent)\n    },\n    \"classification\": {\n      \"producer\": \"ioc-engine\",                // Engine that created/updated this entity\n      \"confidence\": 0.87,                      // 0.0-1.0\n      \"severity\": \"warning\",                   // info | warning | error | critical\n      \"trust_score\": 75,                       // 0-100 (from pkg/trust)\n      \"tags\": [\"osint\", \"malicious\", \"dns\"],   // Arbitrary classification tags\n      \"tlp\": \"amber\",                          // TLP: red | amber | green | white\n      \"pap\": \"amber\"                           // PAP: red | amber | green | white\n    },\n    \"properties\": {\n      // Domain-specific properties — schema varies by entity.type\n      \"domain\": \"suspicious-domain.io\",\n      \"ip_address\": \"45.33.22.1\",\n      \"asn\": \"AS12345\",\n      \"registrar\": \"Namecheap\",\n      \"registration_date\": \"2026-01-15\",\n      \"dns_records\": [\"A\", \"NS\", \"MX\"],\n      \"nameservers\": [\"ns1.suspicious-domain.io\"]\n    },\n    \"spatial\": {\n      // Present only for entity.type = location | geospatial_point | asset\n      \"latitude\": 48.8566,\n      \"longitude\": 2.3522,\n      \"geo_hash\": \"u09tvq\",                    // Geohash for spatial indexing\n      \"country\": \"FR\",\n      \"city\": \"Paris\",\n      \"location_type\": \"satellite_detection\"   // satellite | gps | wifi | manual\n    },\n    \"graph\": {\n      // Graph context — populated by Graph Engine\n      \"degree\": 12,                            // Number of relationships from this entity\n      \"communities\": [\"apt_group_a\", \"infra_cluster_7\"], // Detected communities\n      \"centrality\": 0.73,                      // Betweenness centrality (0-1)\n      \"last_graph_update\": \"2026-06-17T12:30:00Z\"\n    },\n    \"threat\": {\n      // Threat context — populated by Threat Engine\n      \"threat_score\": 87,                      // 0-100 composite score\n      \"threat_score_components\": {\n        \"ioc_match\": 95,\n        \"graph_proximity\": 72,\n        \"ai_analysis\": 84,\n        \"historical\": 78\n      },\n      \"mitre_attack\": [\"T1071\", \"T1105\"],     // MITRE ATT&CK techniques\n      \"kill_chain_phase\": \"delivery\",          // Lockheed Martin kill chain\n      \"attribution\": \"APT-34\",                 // Attributed threat actor (if known)\n      \"active_incidents\": [\"INC-004\"]          // Linked incident IDs\n    },\n    \"analytics\": {\n      // AI context — populated by AI Engine\n      \"ai_summary\": \"Domain registered 2 weeks ago, resolves to VPS hosting 12 other suspicious domains. Pattern matches known APT infrastructure.\",\n      \"ai_analysis_version\": \"2.1.0\",\n      \"correlation_ids\": [\"corr_01J2ABC...\"],  // AI correlations\n      \"anomaly_score\": 0.92, \"ioc_type\": \"domain\",                    // domain | ip | url | hash | email\n      \"ioc_value\": \"suspicious-domain.io\",\n      \"ioc_source\": \"shodan\",\n      \"ioc_feed\": \"osiris-threat-feed-v2\",\n      \"matched_rules\": [\"suspicious-tld\", \"recent-registration\", \"vps-hosting\"],\n      \"ioc_first_seen\": \"2026-06-17T12:00:00Z\"\n    },\n    \"source\": {\n      \"original_source\": \"geoint-sensor-1\",    // Original data source\n      \"source_type\": \"satellite_overpass\",     // Type of source\n      \"provenance\": [                          // Chain of custody\n        {\"engine\": \"soc-stream\", \"timestamp\": \"2026-06-17T12:00:00Z\"},\n        {\"engine\": \"ioc-engine\", \"timestamp\": \"2026-06-17T12:00:05Z\"},\n        {\"engine\": \"ai-engine\", \"timestamp\": \"2026-06-17T12:00:30Z\"}\n      ],\n      \"raw_data\": {}                           // Original raw data (optional)\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n### 2.2 Entity Type Hierarchy\n\n```\nEntity (root)\n├── Observable\n│   ├── domain              e.g., suspicious-domain.io\n│   ├── ip_address          e.g., 45.33.22.1\n│   ├── url                 e.g., https://[REDACTED:PASSWORD]@evil.com\n│   ├── phone               e.g., +33612345678\n│   └── crypto_wallet       e.g., bc1q...\n├── Threat Actor\n│   ├── individual          e.g., \"APT-34 operative\"\n│   ├── group               e.g., \"APT-34\"\n│   └── organization        e.g., \"Iranian MABNA Institute\"\n├── Incident\n│   ├── security_incident   e.g., \"Data breach at corp-X\"\n│   └── intrusion_set       e.g., \"Operation DustStorm\"\n├── Location\n│   ├── geospatial_point    e.g., 48.8566, 2.3522\n│   ├── region              e.g., \"Paris metropolitan\"\n│   ├── country             e.g., \"France\"\n│   └── facility            e.g., \"Data center OVH Gravelines\"\n├── Asset\n│   ├── device              e.g., \"CCTV camera Paris-12\"\n│   ├── vessel              e.g., \"Cargo ship MSC Zoe\"\n│   ├── aircraft            e.g., \"Boeing 737, reg F-GZNE\"\n│   └── satellite           e.g., \"Sentinel-2\"\n├── Signal\n│   ├── communication       e.g., \"Radio intercept 433MHz\"\n│   ├── radar               e.g., \"Surface radar return\"\n│   └── electronic          e.g., \"ELINT signal pattern X\"\n├── Malware\n│   ├── family              e.g., \"Emotet\"\n│   ├── sample              e.g., \"SHA256:3f7c...\"\n│   └── campaign            e.g., \"Phishing wave June 2026\"\n└── Tool\n    ├── c2_framework        e.g., \"Cobalt Strike\"\n    ├── exploit_kit         e.g., \"Angler EK\"\n    └── vulnerability       e.g., \"CVE-2026-1234\"\n```\n\n### 2.3 Event Model\n\n```json\n{\n  \"osiris:event:v2\": {\n    \"identity\": {\n      \"event_id\": \"evt_01J2XYZ...\",\n      \"correlation_id\": \"corr_01J2XYZ...\",\n      \"event_type\": \"osiris.soc.raw.ingested\"\n    },\n    \"entity\": {\n      \"entity_id\": \"ent_01J2XYZ...\",   // Links to the entity this event is about\n      \"entity_type\": \"domain\"\n    },\n    \"payload\": {\n      // Event-specific payload (differs from entity properties)\n      \"source\": \"soc-stream-gateway\",\n      \"raw_log\": \"...\",\n      \"normalized\": { ... }\n    },\n    \"context\": {\n      \"investigation_id\": \"inv_01J2ABC...\",\n      \"triggered_by\": \"ioc-engine\",\n      \"pipeline_stage\": 1\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n### 2.4 Relation Model\n\n```json\n{\n  \"osiris:relation:v2\": {\n    \"source_id\": \"ent_01J2XYZ...\",       // Source entity\n    \"target_id\": \"ent_01J2XYY...\",       // Target entity\n    \"relation_type\": \"resolves_to\",      // resolves_to | owned_by | communicates_with |\n                                         // located_at | attributed_to | variant_of |\n                                         // detected_by | analyzed_by\n    \"weight\": 0.95,                       // 0-1 relationship strength\n    \"discovered_by\": \"ioc-engine\",        // Engine that discovered this relation\n    \"first_seen\": \"2026-06-17T12:00:00Z\",\n    \"last_seen\": \"2026-06-17T12:34:56Z\",\n    \"properties\": {\n      \"protocol\": \"DNS\",\n      \"confidence\": 0.87\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n---\n\n## 3. Intelligence Pipeline Flow\n\n### 3.1 Full Investigation Pipeline\n\n```\n                    INTELLIGENCE PIPELINE\n                    ═════════════════════\n\n    RAW DATA                    ENRICHMENT                    INTELLIGENCE\n    ────────                    ──────────                    ────────────\n\n    SOC Stream ──────┐\n    (1000 evts/s)     │\n                     ├──→ IOC Engine ──→ AI Engine ──→ Graph Engine ──→ Threat Engine ──→ UI\n    Sensors ─────────┘        │             │              │                │\n    (Shodan/OpenSky)          │             │              │                │\n                              ▼             ▼              ▼                ▼\n                         [IoC Matches]  [Correlations]  [Graph Store]   [Alert/Score]\n                              │             │              │                │\n                              ▼             ▼              ▼                ▼\n                      ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n                      │              ENTITY FUSION (per entity)              │\n                      │                                                      │\n                      │  Entity {                                           │\n                      │    identity: { type: \"domain\", label: \"evil.com\" }  │\n                      │    ioc: { matched_rules: [...] }                    │\n                      │    analytics: { ai_summary: \"...\", anomaly: 0.92 }  │\n                      │    graph: { degree: 12, communities: [...] }        │\n                      │    threat: { score: 87, mitre: [...] }             │\n                      │    spatial: { country: \"FR\", city: \"Paris\" }       │\n                      │  }                                                  │\n                      └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n                                     │\n                                     ▼\n                              ┌──────────────┐\n                              │    Search     │── Index entity → UI Search\n                              │    Engine     │\n                              └──────────────┘\n                                     │\n                                     ▼\n                              ┌──────────────┐\n                              │  Workflow    │── Trigger investigation workflow\n                              │  Engine      │\n                              └──────────────┘\n```\n\n### 3.2 Pipeline Stages\n\n| Stage | Engine | Duration | Output | Event |\n|-------|--------|----------|--------|-------|\n| **1. Ingestion** | SOC Stream / Sensors | <10ms | Raw event | `osiris.soc.raw` |\n| **2. Normalization** | IOC Engine | <50ms | Normalized entity | `osiris.intel.entity` |\n| **3. IOC Matching** | IOC Engine | <100ms | Matched IoCs | `osiris.ioc.match` |\n| **4. AI Analysis** | AI Engine | <2s | Correlations, summary | `osiris.ai.correlation` |\n| **5. Graph Storage** | Graph Engine | <500ms | Node + edges | `osiris.graph.update` |\n| **6. Threat Scoring** | Threat Engine | <200ms | Threat score | `osiris.threat.score` |\n| **7. Alert Generation** | Threat Engine | <100ms | Alert/Incident | `osiris.threat.alert` |\n| **8. Search Indexing** | Search Engine | <500ms | Searchable entity | `osiris.search.result` |\n| **9. UI Update** | Frontend WS | <100ms | Panel update | WebSocket push |\n\n**End-to-end latency target (SOC event → UI):** <3.5s (P99)\n\n### 3.3 Pipeline Priority Levels\n\n```\nCRITICAL PATH (threat detection):          SOC → IOC → Threat → Alert → UI\n   SLA: <500ms for known IoCs\n   SLA: <5s for AI-assisted analysis\n\nNORMAL PATH (entity enrichment):           SOC → IOC → AI → Graph → Search → UI\n   SLA: <10s end-to-end\n\nBACKGROUND PATH (batch analytics):         Sensors → GEOINT → Graph → AI → Fusion → UI\n   SLA: <60s for spatial data\n\nBATCH PATH (historical analysis):          Query → AI → Graph → Threat → Report\n   SLA: <5min for complex correlations\n```\n\n---\n\n## 4. Graph Integration Strategy\n\n### 4.1 Graph-First Architecture\n\n```\n┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│                     GRAPH-FIRST ARCHITECTURE                              │\n│                                                                          │\n│  The Knowledge Graph (Memgraph) is the CENTRAL DATA STORE.              │\n│  Every entity and every relationship lives in the graph.                 │\n│  All other engines read from and write to the graph.                     │\n│                                                                          │\n│  ┌──────────┐     ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐               │\n│  │   All    │────▶│                                      │               │\n│  │  Engines │     │          KNOWLEDGE GRAPH              │               │\n│  └──────────┘     │          (Memgraph + Cypher)          │               │\n│                   │                                      │               │\n│                   │  ┌────────────────────────────────┐  │               │\n│                   │  │  Entity Nodes                    │  │               │\n│                   │  │  (domain, IP, person, location, │  │               │\n│                   │  │   threat_actor, malware, ...)    │  │               │\n│                   │  └────────────────────────────────┘  │               │\n│                   │                                      │               │\n│                   │  ┌────────────────────────────────┐  │               │\n│                   │  │  Relationship Edges              │  │               │\n│                   │  │  (resolves_to, communicates_with,│  │               │\n│                   │  │   located_at, attributed_to, ...)│  │               │\n│                   │  └────────────────────────────────┘  │               │\n│                   │                                      │               │\n│                   │  ┌────────────────────────────────┐  │               │\n│                   │  │  Event Log (time-series)         │  │               │\n│                   │  │  (event_id → entity_id,          │  │               │\n│                   │  │   timestamp-sorted)              │  │               │\n│                   │  └────────────────────────────────┘  │               │\n│                   └──────────────────────────────────────┘               │\n│                              │                                           │\n│                              ▼                                           │\n│  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │\n│  │                    GRAPH QUERY PATTERNS                           │   │\n│  │                                                                   │   │\n│  │  1. Entity View:   MATCH (n) WHERE n.id = $id RETURN n           │   │\n│  │  2. Neighborhood:  MATCH (n)-[r]-(m) WHERE n.id = $id RETURN n,r,m│   │\n│  │  3. Path Finding:  MATCH p = SHORTESTPATH((a)-[*]-(b)) RETURN p  │   │\n│  │  4. Community:     MATCH (n)-[*1..3]-(m) WHERE n.tag = $tag      │   │\n│  │  5. Time Series:   MATCH (e:Event) WHERE e.time > $t RETURN e    │   │\n│  │  6. Threat Proximity: MATCH (n)-[*]-(t:ThreatActor) RETURN n     │   │\n│  │  7. Pattern Match: MATCH (d:Domain)-->(i:IP)-->(m:Malware)       │   │\n│  │  8. Centrality:    CALL betweenness_centrality()                  │   │\n│  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │\n│                                                                          │\n└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n```\n\n### 4.2 Graph Event Flow\n\n```\n     Engine writes to graph via Event Bus (not direct DB access):\n     ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n     1. AI Engine:  \"osiris.intel.entity.created\" { entity }\n        → Graph Worker consumes → MERGE (n:Entity {id: entity.id})\n        → Event: \"osiris.graph.update\" { node_id: entity.id }\n\n     2. IOC Engine: \"osiris.ioc.match\" { source_id, target_id, relation }\n        → Graph Worker consumes → MATCH (s),(t) MERGE (s)-[r:RESOLVES_TO]->(t)\n        → Event: \"osiris.graph.edge\" { source_id, target_id, relation_type }\n\n     3. GEOINT Engine: \"osiris.geoint.processed\" { entity }\n        → Graph Worker consumes → MERGE (n:Entity {id: entity.id})\n        → Adds spatial properties → Event: \"osiris.graph.update\"\n\n     4. Threat Engine: \"osiris.threat.score\" { entity_id, score }\n        → Graph Worker consumes → SET n.threat_score = score\n        → Event: \"osiris.graph.update\" { node_id: entity_id, threat_score }\n\n     All reads happen through Graph Query API:\n     ─────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n     UI Panel → \"osiris.graph.query\" { query_type, params }\n     → Graph Engine consumes → Executes Cypher → \"osiris.graph.result\"\n     → UI Panel receives result\n```\n\n### 4.3 Graph Schema\n\n```cypher\n// Node Labels\nCREATE CONSTRAINT ON (n:Entity) ASSERT n.id IS UNIQUE;\nCREATE CONSTRAINT ON (n:Domain) ASSERT n.id IS UNIQUE;\nCREATE CONSTRAINT ON (n:IPAddress) ASSERT n.id IS UNIQUE;\nCREATE CONSTRAINT ON (n:ThreatActor) ASSERT n.id IS UNIQUE;\nCREATE CONSTRAINT ON (n:Incident) ASSERT n.id IS UNIQUE;\nCREATE CONSTRAINT ON (n:Location) ASSERT n.id IS UNIQUE;\nCREATE CONSTRAINT ON (n:Event) ASSERT n.id IS UNIQUE;\n\n// Edge Types\n// :RESOLVES_TO     — domain → IP, URL → domain\n// :OWNED_BY        — domain → registrar, IP → ASN\n// :COMMUNICATES_WITH — entity → entity (network traffic)\n// :LOCATED_AT      — entity → location (geospatial)\n// :ATTRIBUTED_TO   — entity → threat actor\n// :VARIANT_OF      — malware → malware family\n// :DETECTED_BY     — entity → IOC rule, entity → sensor\n// :ANALYZED_BY     — entity → AI analysis\n// :RELATED_TO      — generic relationship\n// :PART_OF         — entity → incident, entity → campaign\n// :TRIGGERED       — event → entity, event → incident\n\n// Time-Series Events stored as Event nodes with :OCCURRED_AT edges to entities\n// Events are timestamped for temporal queries and replay\n```\n\n---\n\n## 5. Real-Time Enrichment Model\n\n### 5.1 Enrichment Pipeline\n\n```\n┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│                    REAL-TIME ENRICHMENT MODEL                             │\n│                                                                          │\n│  Every entity goes through progressive enrichment as data arrives:       │\n│                                                                          │\n│  ENTITY CREATED (minimal)                                                │\n│  ├── entity_id, type, label, source                                      │\n│  ├── confidence: initial (from source)                                   │\n│  ├── tlp: inherits from source                                           │\n│  └── tags: [source_detected]                                             │\n│         │                                                                 │\n│         ▼                                                                │\n│  ENRICHMENT STAGE 1 — IOC Engine (100ms)                                 │\n│  ├── Check against all IOC feeds                                         │\n│  ├── If match: add ioc section, increase confidence                     │\n│  ├── Add tags: [ioc_matched, feed_name]                                  │\n│  └── Publish: osiris.ioc.match → triggers Stage 2                       │\n│         │                                                                 │\n│         ▼                                                                │\n│  ENRICHMENT STAGE 2 — AI Engine (1-5s)                                   │\n│  ├── AI analysis: summary, anomaly score, classification                │\n│  ├── Entity resolution: merge with existing entities                     │\n│  ├── Correlation: find related events/entities                           │\n│  ├── Add tags: [ai_analyzed, ai_classification]                          │\n│  └── Publish: osiris.ai.correlation → triggers Stage 3                  │\n│         │                                                                 │\n│         ▼                                                                │\n│  ENRICHMENT STAGE 3 — Graph Engine (500ms)                               │\n│  ├── Store entity as graph node                                          │\n│  ├── Create edges from enriched relations                                │\n│  ├── Compute centrality, community detection                             │\n│  ├── Add tags: [graph_stored, community_name]                            │\n│  └── Publish: osiris.graph.update → triggers Stage 4                    │\n│         │                                                                 │\n│         ▼                                                                │\n│  ENRICHMENT STAGE 4 — Threat Engine (200ms)                              │\n│  ├── Compute threat score (IOC + AI + graph proximity)                   │\n│  ├── Check MITRE ATT&CK mapping                                          │\n│  ├── If score > threshold: create alert                                  │\n│  ├── Add tags: [scored, threat_level]                                    │\n│  └── Publish: osiris.threat.score + osiris.threat.alert (if triggered)  │\n│         │                                                                 │\n│         ▼                                                                │\n│  ENRICHMENT STAGE 5 — Search Engine (500ms)                              │\n│  ├── Index fully enriched entity for search                              │\n│  ├── Make discoverable via UI search                                     │\n│  └── Publish: osiris.search.result → Frontend WS                        │\n│         │                                                                 │\n│         ▼                                                                │\n│  ENRICHMENT STAGE 6 — Workflow Engine (if investigation mode)            │\n│  ├── Check if entity triggers investigation rules                        │\n│  ├── If yes: create investigation, open incident                         │\n│  └── Publish: osiris.cp.workflow.triggered                               │\n│                                                                          │\n│  TOTAL PIPELINE LATENCY: ~7s for full enrichment                         │\n│  TARGET: <3.5s for critical path (skip AI for known patterns)            │\n│                                                                          │\n└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n```\n\n### 5.2 Incremental Enrichment\n\n```json\n{\n  \"incremental_enrichment\": {\n    \"principle\": \"Entities are never 'done'. Every new data source triggers re-enrichment.\",\n    \"triggers\": [\n      {\"event\": \"osiris.ioc.feed.updated\", \"action\": \"recheck_all_matched_entities\"},\n      {\"event\": \"osiris.threat.score.changed\", \"action\": \"reanalyze_entity(entity_id)\"},\n      {\"event\": \"osiris.graph.community_updated\", \"action\": \"recalculate_proximity_scores\"},\n      {\"event\": \"osiris.geoint.track.updated\", \"action\": \"update_spatial_properties(entity_id)\"},\n      {\"event\": \"osiris.intel.correlation.found\", \"action\": \"merge_entity_correlations\"}\n    ],\n    \"cooldown\": {\n      \"per_entity\": 60000,       // Minimum 60s between re-enrichments of same entity\n      \"per_source\": 300000       // Minimum 5min between same-source re-checks\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n---\n\n## 6. Conflict Resolution Strategy\n\n### 6.1 Conflict Types\n\n| Conflict | Example | Resolution |\n|----------|---------|------------|\n| **Identity conflict** | Two engines create entities for the same real-world object with different IDs | Entity resolution via fusing engine (pkg/fusion) — merge IDs, keep oldest, add alias |\n| **Property conflict** | AI Engine says confidence=0.87, IOC Engine says confidence=0.65 | Trust-score weighted average: final = Σ(trust_i × value_i) / Σ(trust_i) |\n| **Relation conflict** | IOC Engine adds edge A→B, AI Engine adds edge A→B with different type | Keep both edges with different relation_type. If type same, keep highest weight |\n| **Tag conflict** | GEOINT tags \"active\", Threat tags \"inactive\" | Last-writer-wins with timestamp. Both tags kept, latest wins for semantic meaning |\n| **Score conflict** | Threat Engine score=87, AI Engine predicted score=92 | Composite score = 0.7 × threat + 0.3 × ai_prediction. Components stored separately |\n| **Label conflict** | SOC says \"suspicious-domain.io\", OSINT says \"legit-domain.com\" | Entity resolution detects same entity → keep both labels as aliases. Primary label = highest confidence source |\n| **Deletion conflict** | Engine A marks entity deleted, Engine B updates it 1s later | Tombstone wins. Deleted entities have TTL. # Engine Integration Architecture Delivered — `frontend/ENGINE-INTEGRATION-ARCHITECTURE.md`

## Architecture Deliverable (7 Sections, 724 lines)

| Section | Status | Content |
|---------|--------|---------|
| **1. Engine Interaction Model** | ✅ | No direct coupling rule, 6 interaction patterns (event-driven, request/response, pipeline, fan-out, aggregate, feedback), full event type mapping across all 6 engines |
| **2. Shared Data Schema (Entity-Centric)** | ✅ | Master Entity Model (10 sections: identity, temporal, classification, properties, spatial, graph, threat, analytics, ioc, source), Entity Type Hierarchy (10 root types), Event Model, Relation Model |
| **3. Intelligence Pipeline Flow** | ✅ | 6-stage enrichment pipeline (IOC → AI → Graph → Threat → Search → Workflow), 9 pipeline stages with latency targets, 4 priority tiers (critical <500ms → batch <5min) |
| **4. Graph Integration Strategy** | ✅ | Graph-first architecture (Memgraph central data store), 8 Cypher query patterns, event-driven graph writes, full Graph Schema with constraints and edge types |
| **5. Real-Time Enrichment Model** | ✅ | 6-stage progressive enrichment, incremental enrichment with 5 triggers + cooldown policy |
| **6. Conflict Resolution Strategy** | ✅ | 7 conflict types with resolutions, 5×5 Conflict Resolution Matrix (all engine pairs), Last-Writer-Wins with provenance tracking |
| **7. Summary** | ✅ | 10-component table + 7 key design decisions |

## Key Design Decisions

| Decision | Rationale |
|----------|-----------|
| **Graph-first** | Memgraph already deployed; graph enables traversal, proximity, path finding |
| **No direct coupling** | Event Bus exclusively — engines can be replaced/scaled independently |
| **Entity-centric model** | Single source of truth; every intelligence object is an Entity with unique ULID |
| **Provenance tracking** | Every property knows who set it when — enables audit, rollback, resolution |
| **Trust-weighted conflict resolution** | Composite scores weighted by engine trust level, not averaged equally |
| **6-stage pipeline** | Parallelism with dependency ordering (IOC before AI, Graph before Threat) |
| **Incremental enrichment** | Entities never "done" — reactive re-enrichment on every new data source |

Strategy\n\n```json\n{\n  \"state_sync\": {\n    \"principle\": \"Server is source of truth. Client caches aggressively, invalidates lazily.\",\n    \"invalidation\": {\n      \"entities\": \"TTL 60s, full refresh on investigation focus change\",\n      \"graph\": \"TTL 30s, live updates via WS event\",\n      \"threat_scores\": \"TTL 10s, push on change via WS\",\n      \"search_results\": \"No cache — fresh on every query\",\n      \"ui_state\": \"Persistent to localStorage (panel layout, investigation)\"\n    },\n    \"optimistic_updates\": {\n      \"search_queries\": \"Immediate local result from entity store, backend updates on arrival\",\n      \"panel_docking\": \"Immediate UI update, no server confirm needed\",\n      \"entity_create\": \"Local only until backend confirms\"\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n---\n\n## 3. Real-Time Data Strategy\n\n### 3.1 WebSocket vs SSE Decision\n\n| Criteria | WebSocket | SSE (Server-Sent Events) |\n|----------|-----------|--------------------------|\n| **Bidirectional** | ✅ Yes (needed for graph queries, AI requests) | ❌ No (server→client only) |\n| **Connection overhead** | Higher (HTTP upgrade) | Lower (standard HTTP) |\n| **Auto-reconnect** | Manual implementation | Built-in (EventSource) |\n| **Browser support** | ✅ Universal | ✅ Universal (except IE) |\n| **Message types** | Binary + Text | Text-only |\n| **Multiplexing** | Single connection, multiple channels via sub-protocol | Single connection, one event stream |\n| **Backpressure** | Manual | Automatic (HTTP/2 flow control) |\n| **Existing infrastructure** | ✅ `pkg/stream` + `backend WS` + `useWebSocket` hook | ❌ Not deployed |\n\n**Decision: WebSocket primary, SSE fallback.**\n\nWebSocket is required for bidirectional communication (graph queries, AI inference requests). The existing `pkg/stream` WebSocket hub already supports this. SSE would be used as a read-only fallback for environments where WebSocket is blocked.\n\n### 3.2 Real-Time Architecture\n\n```\n┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│                    REAL-TIME DATA STRATEGY                            │\n├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n│                                                                     │\n│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │\n│  │  WEBSOCKET MANAGER (Singleton)                               │   │\n│  │  ─────────────────────────────                               │   │\n│  │                                                               │   │\n│  │  Connection lifecycle:                                        │   │\n│  │  1. Connect to /ws/events (backend)                          │   │\n│  │  2. Authenticate (send JWT)                                  │   │\n│  │  3. Subscribe to channels:                                    │   │\n│  │     - \"events\" — SOC/OSINT events                            │   │\n│  │     - \"graph\" — graph updates                                 │   │\n│  │     - \"geoint\" — spatial updates                              │   │\n│  │     - \"threat\" — threat alerts                                │   │\n│  │     - \"system\" — health/heartbeat                             │   │\n│  │  4. Heartbeat every 30s                                      │   │\n│  │  5. Reconnect on close (exponential backoff: 1s→5s→30s)     │   │\n│  │                                                               │   │\n│  │  Multiplexing strategy:                                       │   │\n│  │  - Single WS connection (one TCP socket)                     │   │\n│  │  - All channels multiplexed over one connection              │   │\n│  │  - Each message has \"channel\" field in JSON envelope         │   │\n│  │  - WebSocket Manager routes to subscribers by channel        │   │\n│  │                                                               │   │\n│  │  Message format:                                              │   │\n│  │  {                                                           │   │\n│  │    \"channel\": \"events\",                                      │   │\n│  │    \"type\": \"osiris.intel.entity.created\",                    │   │\n│  │    \"payload\": { ... },                                       │   │\n│  │    \"timestamp\": \"2026-06-17T12:34:56Z\"                      │   │\n│  │  }                                                           │   │\n│  │                                                               │   │\n│  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │\n│                                                                     │\n│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │\n│  │  CHANNEL SUBSCRIPTION MODEL                                   │   │\n│  │  ────────────────────────────                                 │   │\n│  │                                                               │   │\n│  │  Panel subscribes to channel on mount:                        │   │\n│  │  → GraphPanel subscribes to \"graph\" channel                  │   │\n│  │  → GeointPanel subscribes to \"geoint\" channel                │   │\n│  │  → ThreatPanel subscribes to \"threat\" channel                │   │\n│  │  → EventStream subscribes to \"events\" channel                │   │\n│  │  → TopBar subscribes to \"system\" channel                     │   │\n│  │                                                               │   │\n│  │  On channel message received:                                 │   │\n│  │  1. WebSocket Manager deserializes message                   │   │\n│  │  2. Calls all subscribed callbacks                            │   │\n│  │  3. Each callback updates local store                         │   │\n│  │  4. React re-renders affected components                      │   │\n│  │                                                               │   │\n│  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │\n│                                                                     │\n│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │\n│  │  OFFLINE / RECONNECT STRATEGY                                │   │\n│  │  ─────────────────────────────                               │   │\n│  │                                                               │   │\n│  │  1. Connection lost → show \"Reconnecting...\" indicator       │   │\n│  │  2. Buffer outgoing messages (max 100)                       │   │\n│  │  3. Exponential backoff: 1s → 2s → 5s → 10s → 30s (max)    │   │\n│  │  4. On reconnection:                                         │   │\n│  │     a. Re-authenticate                                       │   │\n│  │     b. Flush buffered outgoing messages                       │   │\n│  │     c. Request missed events (since last known event_id)     │   │\n│  │     d. Resume normal operation                               │   │\n│  │                                                               │   │\n│  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │\n│                                                                     │\n└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n```\n\n### 3.3 Data Fetching Strategy\n\n```typescript\n// Synchronous data fetching pattern (graph queries, AI requests, search):\n// 1. Publish request to WebSocket with correlation_id + callback\n// 2. Subscribe to response channel\n// 3. On response, match correlation_id → resolve callback\n// 4. Timeout after 30s → reject callback\n\ninterface PendingRequest {\n  correlation_id: string\n  resolve: (data: unknown) => void\n  reject: (error: Error) => void\n  timeout: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout>\n  created_at: number\n}\n\n// Request/Response via WebSocket:\n// Send:    { channel: \"graph\", type: \"query\", correlation_id: \"req_abc\", payload: { ... } }\n// Receive: { channel: \"graph\", type: \"result\", correlation_id: \"req_abc\", payload: { ... } }\n```\n\n---\n\n## 4. \"graph_relations\": \"Load 1-hop neighbors on node click, 2-hop on expand\",\n      \"events\": \"Load last 100 on mount, stream new ones via WS\",\n      \"threat_scores\": \"Load all visible entities, update via WS\"\n    },\n    \"pagination\": {\n      \"search\": \"Cursor-based pagination (cursor=entity_id, limit=50)\",\n      \"events\": \"Time-based pagination (before=timestamp, limit=100)\",\n      \"graph\": \"BFS-based expansion (start=node_id, depth=1, limit=500)\"\n    },\n    \"caching\": {\n      \"entity_store\": \"Local cache (Zustand), TTL 60s\",\n      \"graph_queries\": \"LRU cache (max 50 queries), invalidated on graph updates\",\n      \"search_results\": \"No cache (fresh on every query)\",\n      \"map_tiles\": \"Browser cache (Mapbox tiles, 7 days)\"\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n### 6.3 Memory Management\n\n```json\n{\n  \"memory_management\": {\n    \"entity_store\": \"Max 50,000 entities (evict oldest when exceeded)\",\n    \"event_buffer\": 20 inspected entities\",\n    \"ws_message_buffer\": \"Max 1000 unprocessed messages\",\n    \"tile_cache\": \"Browser managed (Mapbox ~50MB)\",\n    \"total_target\": \"<200MB RAM in normal \"chunks\": [\n        \"shell.js (150KB) — TopBar, Sidebar, Canvas, Inspector\",\n        \"graph-panel.js (200KB) — ReactFlow, graph visualization\",\n        \"geoint-panel.js (300KB) — Deck.gl,
